newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia attacks Portugal role as Timor defender.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia attacks Portugal role as Timor defender.

text.p: Indonesia on Wednesday attacked Portugal's posture as defender of the rights of people in its former colony of East Timor, saying Lisbon had the worst record as a coloniser and decoloniser of any nation.
Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas condemned a television appearance by Portugese President Jorge Sampaio, who criticised Jakarta's policy on East Timor.
Sampaio was speaking after two East Timorese jointly received the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize at a ceremony in Oslo on Tuesday night.
"How can the president of a nation which is known throughout the world as the worst coloniser and the worst decoloniser without embarassment struggle for human rights?" Alatas said.
Alatas was speaking to reporters during the annual foreign ministers' meeting of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) in Jakarta.
Portugal withdrew from mainly Catholic East Timor after a 1974 coup in Lisbon overthrew the government there. Indonesia invaded East Timor in December, 1975.

The United Nations has never recognised the takeover and still regards Portugal as the administering power. U.N.-brokered talks between Indonesia and Portugal have so far failed to produce an agreement over the heavily-militarised territory.
Indonesia has been regularly accused of human rights abuses in East Timor since declaring the territory its 27th province in July 1976.

"The President of Portugal is now taking a position as the defender of human rights and a fighter for self-determination. The question is, was the right of self-determination implemented in Angola?" Alatas said.
Portugal pulled out of its African colonies of Angola and Mozambique not long after the 1974 coup in Lisbon.

Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo, who shared the prize jointly with separatist leader Jose Ramos-Horta, called in his acceptance speech on Tuesday for authentic dialogue on the problems of East Timor.
